decisions.reason: As the publicly announced flagship product line close to the core, and central to the digital-practice direction, the firm's heavy investment and visible commitment make withdrawal very unlikely.

The education institute builds on the firm's training resources and customer ties, and pandemic-related weakness in in-person courses can be attributed to temporary causes, so management will persist with it.
Remote screen-sharing support gained relevance with remote work, costs little, and is embedded in the support business, so there is no reason to drop it.

The analytics dashboard was presented on its own page and fits the announced direction toward efficiently managed, connected practices, so management will keep investing in it despite limited visible evidence.
The complete practice bundle packages the core offer for new practices and was visibly promoted, so it is likely kept, perhaps restructured rather than withdrawn.

The listing portal is distant from the core and only mentioned, which makes it the most expendable product, but it costs little and supports the customer community, so commitment likely keeps it alive for now.
